properties.description:
The third "who" axis. AUTHORED_BY says who WROTE something (past tense, never changes); CLAIMS says who is IN it right now (transient, released at checkout); OWNED_BY says whose ground it is, and it survives every session.

BUILT: the edge (`* → Contributor`, with `note` and `since`), a served `owned_by` tool, and the read that makes it earn its keep — loop_status(contributor_id) reports `gaps_on_owned_ground`, each entry naming WHICH owned nodes the gap stands on, and `not_attributable` shrinks by exactly that many.

DELIBERATELY NOT A TRACEABILITY EDGE, the third of a kind after AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS: owning something says who ANSWERS for it, not that a change to it changes them. A Contributor must never appear in a blast radius, and a test asserts it.

⚠️ AND AN UNOWNED NODE RAISES NOTHING. Most of a mature design legitimately has no owner, so absence is ordinary rather than a finding. Whether unowned ground should be detected at all is open in dec:idea-detect-ownership-orphans and turns on a per-project answer to which types are even ownable — a question this capability deliberately does not answer.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN: "is this gap on ground you own?" is a FACT the graph can answer; "should this have an owner?" is a JUDGEMENT it cannot.
properties.name: Whose AREA a node is, recorded durably and read where debt is reported
